newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Rotterdam port dispute approaches resolution -union.
newsitem.headline: Rotterdam port dispute approaches resolution -union.

text.p: The FNV transport union said on Wednesday the prospect of a strike at the port of Rotterdam had faded after it received assurances from labour pool company SHB that it would not carry out forced redundancies.

"There was a negotiation today and a resolution ... an agreement that there will be no forced sackings which conforms to our wishes," said Kees van Nimwegen, the head of the Rotterdam branch of the union.
The agreement also led to the cancellation of a wild-cat strike planned by the works council for Thursday, he said.
The union will continue to meet SHB representatives over the next month.
The dispute centres around plans by SHB's management to make 200 of its 975 employees redundant by the beginning of July and to put 330 workers on a three-day week.

Last week the dispute escalated as some 300 workers launched a wild-cat strike and workers at other companies took limited solidarity action, but the port itself and individual companies were largely unaffected.
SHB said on Wednesday its position was unchanged. The dispute, it said, was more the result of a misunderstanding.
"We made a new statement, but it's the same situation as in January. There was some misunderstanding," said managing director Jan Schermer.
"We will have discussions about the very big problems at our company. We still have to make job cuts," he added.
